فَسِيخٌ [applied to flesh-meat, Parting in pieces, and easily resolvable, by reason of much cooking. (Golius, from Meyd.) ―
-b2- And] (assumed tropical:) A weak man, who becomes unnerved (↓ يَنْفَسِخُ ) on an accasion of difficulty: (L:) a man who does not attain that which he wants, (S, L, K,) and is not fit for his affair, or business; as also ↓ فَسْخٌ [q. v.]. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
